title: Manchester Pub Quiz

questions.q: Which insect has been a symbol of Manchester since the days of the cotton mills?
Which band, formed in Manchester and led by the Gallagher brothers, released "Wonderwall"?
Which long-running ITV soap is set in the fictional town of Weatherfield?
Thanks to its many mills, Victorian Manchester earned which nickname?
The world's first inter-city passenger railway, opened in 1830, linked Manchester with which city?
Which Manchester record label, co-founded by Tony Wilson, released Joy Division and New Order?
The 1819 attack on a peaceful crowd at St Peter's Field is known by what name?
Which suffragette leader, who founded the Women's Social and Political Union in Manchester in 1903, has a statue in St Peter's Square?
Which codebreaker and computer pioneer, who worked at the University of Manchester, is remembered with a statue in Sackville Gardens?
Manchester City's home ground was originally built for which multi-sport event in 2002?

notes: Worker bee adopted as a city emblem during the Industrial Revolution (appears on the 1842 city coat of arms); see Manchester City Council / Wikipedia 'Manchester bee'.
Oasis formed in Manchester in 1991; 'Wonderwall' from (What's the Story) Morning Glory? (1995); see Oasis Wikipedia.
Coronation Street, ITV since 1960, set in fictional Weatherfield (based on Salford); see Coronation Street Wikipedia.
'Cottonopolis' nickname for 19th-century Manchester; see Wikipedia 'Cottonopolis' / Science and Industry Museum.
Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened 15 September 1830; see Wikipedia / Science and Industry Museum (Liverpool Road station).
Factory Records founded 1978 by Tony Wilson and Alan Erasmus; see Factory Records Wikipedia.
Peterloo Massacre, 16 August 1819, St Peter's Field; see Wikipedia 'Peterloo Massacre' / People's History Museum.
Pankhurst founded the WSPU at her Nelson Street home in Manchester in October 1903; statue 'Rise Up, Women' unveiled in St Peter's Square in December 2018; see Pankhurst Centre / Wikipedia.
Alan Turing Memorial statue in Sackville Park (Sackville Gardens), unveiled 2001; Turing worked at the University of Manchester from 1948; see Wikipedia 'Alan Turing Memorial'.
City of Manchester Stadium (now the Etihad) built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games, Man City moved in 2003; see Wikipedia 'City of Manchester Stadium'.
